PART I

Item 1. Business. Acme Corp designs and sells widgets.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our business is subject to a number of risks and uncertainties described below.

Cybersecurity risk. If we are unable to protect our information technology infrastructure against cyberattacks, our business could be harmed.

Supply chain risk. We depend on a limited number of suppliers for critical components used in our products, and disruption to that supply chain could materially affect our results of operations and financial condition in ways that are difficult to predict and mitigate given current global conditions.

Competition risk. The markets in which we compete are highly competitive, and our failure to compete effectively could adversely affect our revenue, margins, and market share over an extended period of time as new entrants continue to emerge.

As discussed elsewhere in this Item 1A. Risk Factors section, our mitigation strategies have been effective to date, though there is no guarantee they will continue to be effective against emerging categories of risk that we have not yet identified or fully assessed.

Regulatory risk. Changes in laws and regulations applicable to our business, including in the jurisdictions where we operate and sell products, could increase our compliance costs or restrict our ability to operate as we currently do, which could materially and adversely affect our financial results in future periods.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Revenue increased 12% year over year, driven primarily by strong demand for our flagship widget product line across all geographic regions in which we operate.

Gross margin expanded due to favorable input cost trends and a richer product mix weighted toward our higher-margin offerings, partially offset by increased freight and logistics costs incurred during the period.
